# StockBar v3.8.1 Release Notes
**Status:** Implemented **Date:** 2026-11-18
With Folync as the portfolio source, total P&L is now measured against the money you paid in, less what you took out, rather than against what the shares you hold cost. This release also fixes when "Updated" says a cached price was fetched, and saves price alerts' last checked prices less often.
## After updating
- **Total P&L changes for a Folync portfolio.** In the portfolio popover and the Overview summary it is now measured against **net deposits** by default. That is the figure Folync's web dashboard shows as "What if not investing". The figure will usually differ from the one shown in 3.8.0. To go back to the old figure, choose **Cost of Current Holdings** in **Settings → General → Measure P&L Against**. - Local and Trading 212 portfolios are not affected. - This version arrives through the updater. Nothing needs doing by hand, apart from allowing Keychain access once after the update, as before.
## Total P&L against net deposits
Total P&L used to be the market value of the shares you hold less what those shares cost. That leaves out cash, sales, dividends, interest and fees, so it is not what the account has made.
For a Folync portfolio, Stockbar now reads net deposits, the money paid in less the money taken out, from Folync's portfolio history. It measures the portfolio value against them, and that value includes cash. An example with invented amounts:
| | Amount | |---|---| | Net deposits | £8,800 | | Shares, at market value | £8,000 | | Cash | £1,600 | | Portfolio value | £9,600 | | What the shares cost | £7,500 | | **P&L against cost of current holdings** | +£500 (+6.67%) | | **P&L against net deposits** | +£800 (+9.09%) |
- **Portfolio popover:** **Total P&L** uses the basis you choose. The box beside it shows **Net Deposits** or **Cost Basis**, with its amount. - **Overview:** when P&L is measured against net deposits, the summary adds **Total P&L** and **Net deposits** rows. It keeps **Unrealised P&L** and **Cost basis**. - **Timing:** net deposits are read at launch and then at most every five minutes. Folync adds a new deposit to its history a minute or two after Trading 212 lists it. Until Stockbar reads it, which takes up to about ten minutes, the deposit counts as gain. **Refresh Now** in Stockbar's Folync settings reads it at once. - **When Folync cannot give net deposits,** for example because its history is missing exchange rates for some transactions, or it cannot be read for fifteen minutes, total P&L is measured against cost basis and the popover box says **Cost Basis**. - **No percentage** is shown when net deposits are zero or negative. - **Not changed:** the menu bar item, which shows the day's change; the per-stock popovers; the Holdings table; the Performance charts; recorded history.
## Settings
- **Settings → General → Measure P&L Against:** **Net Deposits** (the default) or **Cost of Current Holdings**. It is included in Settings export.
## Fixes
- **"Updated" shows when a price was fetched.** The Python helper can serve a price it fetched a few minutes earlier, for example after **Refresh Now**. Stockbar used to stamp it with the time it received it, so "Updated" said "just now" and the history point was recorded at the later time. It now uses the time the price was fetched. - **Price alerts** saved the record of last checked prices once for every alerted symbol whose price moved. They now save it once per refresh, and only when a remembered price changed.
## For developers
- `FolyncNetDeposits` (`FolyncSupplementalData.swift`) takes the last point of the `3m` history's `netContributionSeries`. `refreshFolyncNetDeposits(force:now:)` in `FolyncPortfolioSession.swift` reads it through `routePortfolioHistory` and never uses a history marked stale. `DisplayPortfolioSummary.totalReturn(measuredAgainst:)` chooses the basis; `totalGain` keeps its cost-basis meaning. - Each quote from the Python helper carries `fetchedAt`, which its cache keeps. - The locked Python helper packages were updated (pandas 3.1.1, platformdirs 4.14.5, soupsieve 4.0.1). The pins Stockbar checks at launch are unchanged. - The docs were checked against the app: keyboard shortcuts, Trading 212 defaults, alerts, chart ranges and the Folync and exchange-rate intervals. The README links the [wiki](https://github.com/jayjay181818/StockBar/wiki).

# StockBar v3.8.0 Release Notes
**Status:** Implemented **Date:** 2026-11-17
Stockbar uses less memory and less processor time. It idles in about a fifth less memory, loads its price history at launch in about half the time, and spends about half the processor time on each price refresh. The Python helper that fetches prices now quits when it has been idle for 90 seconds. The figures it shows, the Python pins and the database model are the same as in 3.7.0.
## After updating
- **The Python helper now quits when idle, by default.** **Settings → Advanced → Memory → Quit Python Helper When Idle** is on unless you turn it off. The helper holds 70 MB or more. With the switch on it quits about 90 seconds after its last request, and each refresh starts it again, at about a third of a second of processor time. Turned off, it stays running for 15 minutes after its last request, as in 3.7.0. While markets are open and Stockbar refreshes every minute, it keeps running either way. If you turned the switch off in a testing build, it stays off. - This version arrives through the updater in 3.7.0. Nothing needs doing by hand, apart from allowing Keychain access once after the update, as before.
## Memory and speed
These figures come from the project's benchmark on one Mac, with a made-up portfolio and live price providers turned off. Each change was measured on its own against the version before it, and the first group was also measured together against 3.7.0 on 2026-11-13. The record is in [EXPERIMENTAL_LOG.md](https://github.com/jayjay181818/StockBar/blob/main/EXPERIMENTAL_LOG.md).
- **Idle memory** is about 20% lower: 95.8 MB against 119.9 MB in 3.7.0. That comparison covers the memory and history changes; the refresh changes further down were measured one by one. - **Stored history** is read in batches, away from the main thread, and without each snapshot's positions where they are not needed. Launch to history loaded took 0.63 s against 1.20 s, the benchmark's peak memory during launch is 40 MB lower, and the launch uses about 29% less processor time. - **Each portfolio snapshot** keeps its positions in a compact sorted array, and the price history held in memory is kept in arrays sized to fit. - **Price refreshes** apply all their quotes together, so the main window redraws once per refresh rather than once per symbol. Over four refreshes the app used 3.4 s of processor time against 6.8 s. The processor wakes about a third more often during them, because the figures now get to roll to their new values. - **The Python helper** reads and writes its quote cache once per refresh rather than once per symbol: for 22 symbols, 2 reads of the cache file against 66, and 2 forced writes to disk against 44. - **A symbol's price history** is read only for the time window asked for. The day reads at launch took 11 to 14 ms against about 410 ms. - **History cache files** are no longer rewritten when their value has not changed. - **The portfolio popover** releases its content when it closes, so it is no longer redrawn and its chart reloaded at every refresh while nothing is on screen. - **The session's portfolio snapshots** no longer carry a price for every position, which nothing read. That is up to about 2.3 MB less over a long session with 11 positions, worked out from the sizes of the data. - **Release builds** no longer contain test-coverage counters, which made the app's executable 6.7 MB larger.
## Settings
- **Settings → Advanced → Memory → Quit Python Helper When Idle**, described above. On by default. - **Settings → Advanced → Memory → Roll Digits When Figures Change.** Figures in the main window and the popovers roll to a new value, as before. macOS keeps the digits it draws for this in memory: 6 to 10 MB after the main window's figures have rolled. Turned off, figures change without rolling and that memory is not used. On by default.
## Updates
- **Settings → General → Updates** has a third channel, **Experimental**, beside Stable and Testing. It offers builds of the `experimental` branch, which is used only for major changes, such as an overhaul of the app, or for temporary testing. It can go quiet for long periods, and things may break on it. A release or a testing build reaches it once that branch includes it. - Experimental builds are listed in a feed of their own, so they never appear on Stable or Testing.
## Fixes
- The popover charts no longer draw their line doubling back to the left either side of a gap in time, such as the night between two trading days.
## For developers
- `Scripts/perf/` holds the benchmark: launch, idle and refresh workloads on made-up data, run in turns with `compare.sh`, and a report of each metric's change and whether it is more than run-to-run noise. See `Scripts/README_PERFORMANCE.md`. - `EXPERIMENTAL_LOG.md` records each change of this release with its before and after figures, tests and review, the ideas tried and rejected, and an evaluation of moving parts of the app to Rust. None was moved. - `script/package_release.sh` refuses to package an app built with test-coverage counters. - Branches: ordinary changes go through pull requests into `testing`. `experimental` is used only for major changes or temporary testing. See "Branches, releases and dependencies" in `Docs/Development.md`.

# StockBar v3.7.0 Release Notes
**Status:** Implemented **Date:** 2026-11-11
Stockbar now updates itself, and keeps every credential in one Keychain item so macOS asks for access once after an update, not once per credential. Figures, charts, the Python pins and the database model are the same as in 3.6.0.
## After updating
- **This update is installed by hand**, as before: 3.6.0 and earlier have no updater. Download `Stockbar-3.7.0.zip` from the release page, unzip it and move Stockbar to Applications. Later versions arrive through **Settings → General → Updates**. - **First launch of a downloaded copy**: macOS blocks it until you choose **Open Anyway** in System Settings → Privacy & Security. This is needed once per Mac. Updates installed by Stockbar are not blocked. - **Keychain prompts**: the first launch asks for access to each credential saved by the earlier version, to move it into the new single item. Choose **Always Allow** each time. After later updates macOS asks once. - **Going back to an earlier version** means entering the Folync token, Trading 212 credentials and API keys again: earlier versions do not read the new item.
## Updates
- Stockbar checks for new versions and installs them, using [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). Downloads come from this repository's GitHub releases. An update is installed only if it is signed with Stockbar's update key. - **Settings → General → Updates** has the channel, a switch for automatic checks and **Check Now**. - Two channels: **Stable** receives released versions. **Testing** also receives a build of every change as it is merged, before it is released. Moving from Testing back to Stable takes effect at the next released version. - No profile of your Mac is sent when checking. - Builds are made by GitHub Actions and signed without an Apple developer account. That is why a downloaded copy needs **Open Anyway** once, and why macOS asks for Keychain access again after each update.
## Keychain
- The Folync token and its server, the FMP and Twelve Data API keys and the Trading 212 credentials are kept in one Keychain item, "Stockbar credentials". One item means one prompt after an update. - Credentials saved by earlier versions are imported the first time they are needed. The old items are removed only after the new item has been written and read back. If a prompt is refused, nothing is removed and Stockbar tries again at the next launch. - Checking whether a credential is stored still does not read it, so it never raises a prompt.
## For developers
- A release workflow builds a testing build for every merge into `testing` and a stable release for every version tag, and keeps the signed update feed on the `appcast` branch. See "Release builds and updates" in `Docs/Development.md`. - CI packages the Release build the same way the release workflow does.
